'''Brian David Scalabrine''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|s|k|æ|l|ə|'|b|r|i|n|iː}} {{Respell|SKAL|ə|BREE|nee}}; born March 18, 1978), nicknamed "'''White Mamba'''", is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is currently a television analyst for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is also a [[color commentator|commentator]] for basketball league [[Big3]] and the co-host of "The Starting Lineup" on [[SiriusXM NBA Radio]].

Raised in [[Enumclaw, Washington]], Scalabrine attended the [[University of Southern California]] after transferring from [[Highline College]]. As a member of the [[USC Trojans men's basketball]] team, Scalabrine was the top scorer and a leader in field goals and rebounds. He played at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position in college.

The [[New Jersey Nets]] selected him in the second round of the [[2001 NBA draft]]. The Nets made consecutive [[NBA Finals]] appearances his first two years, and Scalabrine played four seasons with the team. In 2005, he signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] and won a championship with the team in 2008. The Celtics also appeared in the [[2010 NBA Finals]]. Scalabrine signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] the following season, and played with them until 2012. Throughout his NBA career, Scalabrine served as a backup [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]]. Despite never averaging more than 6.3 points per game, Scalabrine became one of the most popular players in the league. 

In 2013, [[Mark Jackson (basketball)|Mark Jackson]] announced that Scalabrine would join his [[Golden State Warriors]] coaching staff. In 2014, Scalabrine took a job as an [[Color commentator|analyst]] for Celtics games on local Boston broadcasts.<ref name="Brian Scalabrine is 'coming home'">{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=Matt|title=Brian Scalabrine is 'coming home'|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24648169/brian-scalabrine-is-coming-home|website=CBS Sports.com|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=6 August 2014}}</ref>

==Early life and college==
Born in [[Long Beach, California]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Deb |first=Sopan |date=2021-04-19 |title=Why the Worst N.B.A. Player Is (Probably) Still Better Than You |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/04/19/sports/basketball/why-the-worst-nba-player-is-probably-still-better-than-you.html |access-date=2025-01-30 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brian Scalabrine Biography |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/bio/_/id/1021/brian-scalabrine |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Scalabrine was one of four children in his family and graduated from [[Enumclaw High School]] at [[Enumclaw, Washington]] in 1996.<ref name="NBA bio"/><ref name="USC"/> He is of Italian ancestry.<ref>{{citation|last=Kirkpatrick|first=Curry|url=https://www.espn.com/magazine/curry_20010323.html|title=Treat me like a fool ...|work=ESPN the Magazine|date=March 23, 2001}}</ref> He enrolled at [[Highline College]] in 1996, played his first year with its basketball team the Thunderbirds, and [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his second year. As a freshman at Highline, Scalabrine averaged 16.3 points, 9.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game. Scalabrine recorded seventeen [[double-double]]s, and led the team in rebounds, blocks, and free throw percentage (75%). The Thunderbirds went 31–1 in the 1996–97 season and won the state junior college championship. Scalabrine was a Northern Division All-Star in 1997 as well as part of the All-[[Northwest Athletic Association of Community Colleges]] Championship Tournament Team.<ref name="USC"/>

In 1998, he transferred to the [[University of Southern California]] (USC). In his first year with the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]], he was the only player to start all 28 games. He led the Trojans in scoring (14.6 points), rebounding (6.4), and field goals (53.1%). In scoring, blocked shots, and field goals, he was also the only [[Pac-10]] conference player among the top 10 players in those areas. His best game performance was against [[American Eagles|American University]] on December 21, 1998: 26 points, seven rebounds, and two blocks.<ref>{{cite web|title=1998–99 Southern California Trojans Schedule and Results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/USC/1999-schedule.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202233247/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/USC/1999-schedule.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 2, 2013|publisher=sports-reference.com|access-date=July 31, 2011}}</ref> On February 13, 1999, he scored 22 points including an important three-pointer in overtime; the unranked USC won an upset victory over number-six [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] 86–82 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 14, 1999 |title=Stanford and U.C.L.A. Are Beaten |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/02/14/sports/college-basketball-men-stanford-and-ucla-are-beaten.html?pagewanted=all |access-date=August 1, 2011 |work=The New York Times|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He was the 1999 Pac-10 Newcomer of the Year and earned an All-Pac-10 honorable mention.<ref name="USC">{{cite web|title=Brian Scalabrine|url=http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/scalabrine_brian00.html|publisher=USC Trojans|year=2001|access-date=July 31, 2011|archive-date=August 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812204148/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/scalabrine_brian00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During his second season with USC, Scalabrine was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] first team and the National Association of Basketball Coaches All-District 15 first team. He also earned a ''[[Sporting News]]'' All-American honorable mention. Again, he finished as USC's top scorer (17.8 ppg) and field goal shooter (53.1%) and was also the second-best Pac-10 scorer. He also made 40.3% of attempted three-pointers. Against the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]], Scalabrine scored 29 points and made 10 rebounds.<ref name="USC"/>

USC advanced to the [[2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament in 2001]], Scalabrine's senior season. In the Elite Eight round, USC lost to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] 79–69; Scalabrine scored 13 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Duke 79, USC 69|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/men/recaps/2001/03/24/dau_uad/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010509093057/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/college/men/recaps/2001/03/24/dau_uad/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 9, 2001|publisher=CNNSI.com|access-date=July 31, 2011|date=March 24, 2001}}</ref> Scalabrine graduated with a degree in history.<ref name="NBA bio"/><ref name="USC"/>

==Professional career==

=== New Jersey Nets (2001–2005) ===
Because he injured his [[fifth metatarsal bone]] during workouts in late September 2001, Scalabrine missed the first ten days of [[New Jersey Nets]] training camp.<ref>{{cite news|last=Robbins|first=Liz|title=Kidd Is Named Captain Before Nets Open Camp|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/10/03/sports/pro-basketball-kidd-is-named-captain-before-nets-open-camp.html?pagewanted=all|access-date=August 1, 2011|newspaper=The New York Times|date=October 3, 2001}}</ref> During the second quarter of the final 2001–02 preseason game, which took place against the [[Detroit Pistons]] on October 26, 2001, Scalabrine again injured his right foot.<ref>{{cite news|last=Robbins|first=Liz|title=A Healthy Nets Team Is Too Much to Wish For|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/10/27/sports/pro-basketball-a-healthy-nets-team-is-too-much-to-wish-for.html|access-date=August 1, 2011|newspaper=The New York Times|date=October 27, 2001}}</ref>  He made his [[NBA]] debut on January 31, 2002, when the Nets played against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref name="NBA bio">{{cite web|title=Brian Scalabrine bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/brian_scalabrine/bio.html|publisher=NBA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101202220100/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/brian_scalabrine/bio.html|archive-date=December 2, 2010}}</ref> As a rookie, Scalabrine averaged 2.1 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 0.8 assists per game.<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web|title=Brian Scalabrine Stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/1021/brian-scalabrine}}</ref> He played in six playoff games his debut season and averaged 0.3 points and 0.5 rebounds.<ref name="NBA bio"/> The Nets were the Eastern Conference Champions of the 2001–02 season and lost the [[2002 NBA Finals]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in four games. In a triple-overtime victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]] in Game 5 of the 2004 Eastern Conference Semifinal series, Scalabrine scored a career high 17 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nets need three overtimes to beat Pistons|url=http://articles.boston.com/2004-05-15/sports/29208077_1_three-overtimes-brian-scalabrine-nets|access-date=July 31, 2011|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=May 15, 2004|agency=Associated Press|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120609203334/http://articles.boston.com/2004-05-15/sports/29208077_1_three-overtimes-brian-scalabrine-nets|archive-date=June 9, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref> He surpassed that high with 29 points on January 26, 2005, against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref name="NBA bio"/> On April 15, 2005, he played a career high 45 minutes.<ref name="NBA stats"/>

During his time with the Nets, Scalabrine gained the nickname "Veal", a play on words based on the dish [[veal]] [[scaloppine]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Stein|first=Marc|title=Favorites of the fans|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=stein_marc&id=1728877|access-date=January 13, 2012|newspaper=espn.com|date=February 6, 2004}}</ref>

=== Boston Celtics (2005–2010) ===
On August 2, 2005, Scalabrine signed a five-year contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Scalabrine signs with Celtics|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2005-08-02-roundup_x.htm|access-date=July 31, 2011|newspaper=USA Today|date=August 2, 2005|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> A month earlier, he and the team agreed on terms that the contract be worth $15 million over the five years.<ref name="Celtics agree">{{cite news|last=Springer|first=Shira|title=Celtics agree with free agent Scalabrine|url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2005/07/08/celtics_agree_with_free_agent_scalabrine/|newspaper=The Boston Globe|date=July 8, 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090611075817/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2005/07/08/celtics_agree_with_free_agent_scalabrine/|archive-date=June 11, 2009}}</ref>

Scalabrine started in nine of 48 games during the 2007–08 season, and played on average 10.7 minutes. He averaged 1.8 points and 1.6 rebounds per game. On April 16, 2008, in the final game of the regular season, Scalabrine tied a season-high with six rebounds and played 29 minutes.  He did not make an appearance in the NBA playoffs.<ref name="NBA bio"/> In the [[2008 NBA Finals]], the Celtics defeated the Lakers in six games.

=== Chicago Bulls (2010–2011) ===
[[File:Brian Scalabrine Bulls.jpg|thumb|alt=An overhead view of Scalabrine on the court|right|Scalabrine warms up before Game 5 of the [[2011 NBA Playoffs#Conference Finals: .281.29 Chicago Bulls vs. .282.29 Miami Heat|2011 Eastern Conference Finals]]]]
On September 21, 2010, Scalabrine agreed to a non-guaranteed contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ys-scalabrinebulls092110|title=Bulls invite Scalabrine to training camp|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|date=September 21, 2010|access-date=July 31, 2011}}</ref> The Bulls visited the Boston Celtics on November 5, 2010, and in double overtime the Bulls won 110–105. Scalabrine played only three minutes that game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Forsberg|first=Chris|title=Celtics sing praises of Brian Scalabrine|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/columns/story?columnist=forsberg_chris&id=5770347|publisher=ESPN|access-date=July 31, 2011|date=November 6, 2010}}</ref> He played 18 games with the Bulls and averaged 1.1 points and 0.4 rebounds per game.<ref name="NBA stats">{{cite web|title=Brian Scalabrine Career State and Totals|url=http://www.nba.com/home/playerfile/brian_scalabrine/career_stats.html|publisher=NBA|access-date=July 31, 2011}}</ref>

===Treviso (2011)===
On September 22, 2011, during the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Scalabrine signed with the Italian team [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]].<ref>{{in lang|it}} [http://www.benettonbasket.it/it/news-8855/motiejunas-in-prestito-al-prokom-scalabrine-e039-nel-roster-attivo-come-039usa039.html MOTIEJUNAS IN PRESTITO AL PROKOM, SCALABRINE E' NEL ROSTER ATTIVO COME 'USA'] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925005334/http://www.benettonbasket.it/it/news-8855/motiejunas-in-prestito-al-prokom-scalabrine-e039-nel-roster-attivo-come-039usa039.html |date=September 25, 2011 }}</ref> He left the team in December 2011 to pursue opportunities in the NBA after the lockout had ended.<ref>[http://www.datasport.it/basket/2011-2012/seriea/basket-benetton-treviso-saluta-scalabrine-seriea.htm La Benetton Treviso saluta Scalabrine].</ref> In 7 league games, he averaged 11.6 points and 5 rebounds, while shooting .545 from the three point range.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Proballers |title=Benetton Treviso Roster, Schedule, Stats (2011-2012) |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/team/163/benetton-treviso/2011 |access-date=2026-07-19 |website=Proballers |language=en}}</ref>
=== Return to Chicago (2011–2012) ===
On December 12, 2011, Scalabrine re-signed with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-re-sign-forward-brian-scalabrine.html | title=Bulls re-sign forward Brian Scalabrine | website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>  During the 2011–12 season, Scalabrine played in 28 games.  In September 2012, he was offered a position as an assistant coach for the Bulls under [[Tom Thibodeau]], but instead opted to become a broadcaster for the Boston Celtics.<ref>[http://www.espn.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/8345043/report-chicago-bulls-brian-scalabrine-retiring-boston-celtics-broadcast-booth Report: Brian Scalabrine retires]</ref>

=== BIG3 League (2017) ===
In 2017, Brian joined the [[Ball Hogs]] of the [[BIG3]] basketball league.

== Coaching career ==
In July 2013, [[Golden State Warriors]] coach [[Mark Jackson (basketball)|Mark Jackson]] announced via [[Twitter]] that Scalabrine was joining his coaching staff.<ref>[https://twitter.com/JacksonMark13/status/354427864193564674 Mark Jackson tweet, July 8, 2013]</ref> During the season, Jackson reassigned Scalabrine to the Warriors' [[D-League]] affiliate after a difference of opinion on the team's direction.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wojnarowski|first1=Adrian|date=March 25, 2014|title=Warriors coach Mark Jackson forces reassignment of assistant Brian Scalabrine|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/warriors-coach-mark-jackson-forces-reassignment-of-assistant-brian-scalabrine-184142899.html|access-date=December 5, 2014|website=Yahoo Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Helin|first1=Kurt|date=August 6, 2014|title=Scalabrine says Mark Jackson didn't push Warriors' players hard enough|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/08/06/scalabrine-says-mark-jackson-didnt-push-warriors-players-hard-enough/|access-date=December 5, 2014|website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

==Broadcasting career==
In September 2012, Scalabrine announced that he had turned down an opportunity to become an assistant coach with the Bulls so that he could join [[Comcast SportsNet New England]] as a commentator. Scalabrine described the job as "a trial run", and said there was a "small possibility" he would resume his playing career overseas in 2013.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--brian-scalabrine-says-he-s-likely-retiring.html Brian Scalabrine says he's likely retiring]</ref>

In 2014, Scalabrine wrote an essay to Boston to announce his "homecoming" to become a [[Comcast SportsNet]] announcer.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2151782-brian-scalabrine-announces-his-return-to-boston-celtics-in-coming-home-essay|title = Brian Scalabrine Announces His Return to Boston Celtics in 'Coming Home' Essay|date = Aug 4, 2014|access-date = Aug 5, 2014|website = Bleacher Report|last = Newport|first = Kyle}}</ref> His essay spoofed a famous ''Sports Illustrated'' story about [[LeBron James]]'s return to Cleveland.<ref name="Brian Scalabrine is 'coming home'"/>

==Personal life==
Scalabrine married Kristen Couch in 2003; their wedding ceremony was held in [[Hawaii]].<ref name="NBA bio"/> They have two children.<ref>{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|title=Scalabrine's wife nixes Thibodeau impersonation|url=http://www.chicagobreakingsports.com/sports/bulls/cbsports-scalabrines-wife-nixes-thibodeau-impersonation-20110501,0,6002015.story|access-date=July 31, 2011|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=May 1, 2011}}</ref> He is also a member of the sports philanthropy organization Athletes for Hope.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brian Scalabrine|url=http://www.athletesforhope.org/brian-scalabrine-allstar.html|publisher=Athletes for Hope|access-date=July 31, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001141856/http://www.athletesforhope.org/brian-scalabrine-allstar.html|archive-date=October 1, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

Scalabrine appeared as himself in an episode of the dark comedy series ''[[Kevin Can F**k Himself]]'' in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crain |first=Caemeron |date=2021-07-11 |title=Kevin Can F**k Himself Episode 6: 'The Grand Victorian' |url=https://tvobsessive.com/2021/07/11/kevin-can-fk-himself-episode-6-the-grand-victorian/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=TV Obsessive |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Fan support ==
Despite his limited playing time, Scalabrine became a popular player. Bulls fans referred to him as "The White Mamba", a play on [[Kobe Bryant]]'s nickname of "The Black Mamba".<ref name="CSN Chicago">{{cite web|title=Return of the 'White Mamba': Bulls re-sign Scalabrine|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/blog/bulls-talk/post/Return-of-the-White-Mamba-Bulls-re-sign-?blockID=610742|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730091857/http://www.csnchicago.com/blog/bulls-talk/post/Return-of-the-White-Mamba-Bulls-re-sign-?blockID=610742|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 30, 2012|publisher=CSN Chicago|year=2011|access-date=January 14, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=January 24, 2011|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/bulls/post/_/id/6750/white-mamba-fan-fave-on-off-the-court|title=White Mamba: Fan fave on, off the court|first=Nick|last=Friedell|date=January 19, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>Wittenstein, Ben. (January 31, 2012). [https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1047970-the-white-mamba-what-makes-people-love-brian-scalabrine "The White Mamba: What Makes People Love Brian Scalabrine"]. ''Bleacher Report''. Retrieved June 12, 2015.</ref>

In 2013, in response to criticism over his bench role throughout his career and to claims that many would beat him one-on-one, Scalabrine stated, "I'm closer to [[LeBron James|LeBron]] than you are to me", suggesting that there is a sizeable difference between any (active or retired) NBA player and those outside the league.
In an event organized by ''[[The Toucher and Rich Show]]'', selected volunteers had the chance to play one-on-one against Scalabrine (until 11 points with a margin of two).
The format was called the "Scallenge" and Scalabrine played four games, one against each of the voluntary contenders.
Scalabrine won every game with a combined score of 44–6.
In an additional game Scalabrine played against the three hosts of the show and won 11–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/toucher-richs-scallenge-no-challenge-for-brian-scalabrine/|title=Toucher & Rich's 'Scallenge' No Challenge For Brian Scalabrine|author=<!--Not stated-->|date=January 22, 2013|website=CBS Boston|access-date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>
